name: Cryptoliths
description: Twisted stones that bend Innistrad's leylines, which Nahiri arranges to hide herself from the Eldrazi-touched monsters.

timeline.summary: Jace finds a twisted monolith on the moor matching those at Markov Manor and in the journal.
timeline.quote: The monolith was unmistakably the same as those he had seen at Markov Manor, the same as he had seen in the journal.

timeline.summary: A spark jumps from the monolith to Jace's hand, and he senses something bright and bell-clear.
timeline.quote: there was a POP and a spark jumped from the end of the monolith to his hand.

timeline.summary: Journal entry 643: the cryptoliths warp mana flow, with potentially severe effects on angels.
timeline.quote: The disruptive properties of the stones appear to also extend to an ability to warp the flow of mana through the region

timeline.summary: Jace sees the Drownyard, a huge ring of jagged stones in the ocean, and realizes all the cryptoliths point to it.
Jace is zapped by a stone again and perceives the Object hovering above the circle, the nexus of Innistrad's redirected leylines.
timeline.quote: A blind spot, the Object, loomed in his vision, hovering just above the circle of stones in the distance.

timeline.summary: Nahiri's ring of ley stones renders her invisible to the monsters, which instead attack the vampires.
timeline.quote: These monsters were blind to her within her ring of ley stones.

relations.note: All the cryptoliths point toward it.

pages_say.description: Twisted stones that manipulate mana flow; a moonfolk planeswalker explains a theory about them in Jace's vision.
Twisted stones with directional energy fields that warp mana flow and all point toward the Drownyard.
Twisted stones that bend Innistrad's leylines, which Nahiri arranges to hide herself from the Eldrazi-touched monsters.
